OP, I do medical billing for a living. 90% of what I deal with is ER visits. I don't know where you live, but around here an ER visit like you describe is a few hundred bucks at most, so I'm a little skeptical that you're reading the bill right. Or you're full of shit. And since you've decided to not post this for a month, my bullshitomitere is pinging pretty high. Now, in case you're not full of it, here's how to help your GF assuming she hasn't already settled this. Find out what ER code was used on her bill. If it was anything other than 99281 for the ER charge, she needs to dispute it because they up-coded the bill. ER codes are 99281-5 depending on severity. 99281 is for piddly shit like 3 stitches, 99285 is for cardiac arrest, broken neck, compound fracture etc. After that, and this may surprise people, getting stitches done counts as a minor surgery. This is where I'm assuming most of the actual cost of the bill comes in as this most likely be coded as "OR services". I know what you're thinking, that doesn't make any sense, she didn't get operated on. Just know that "OR services" is actually just a general term, the code is what matters. Unfortunately I don't know those codes off the top of my head so I would need to know what the coder used to determine it's validity.

Here's another reason why I think OP is most likely a bundle of sticks trying to start a circle-jerk out of boredom. Even if his GF has the absolute most shit-tier health insurance available there is no fucking way that after her insurance processed the claim the bill would be 5k. The only way that could happen is if the hospital is out-of-network with her health plan and the insurance won't cover it. In which case it's her own fault for not checking first. If it was in-network, and if she's with a major carrier most hospitals would be, then insurance company contracts with hospitals have case-rate pricing for ER services. I'm making a generalization here but I feel justified in doing so from my experience. All 3 dozen or so hospitals I do billing for have case-rate pricing for ER services with all the major health insurance carriers. Case rates will vary depending on the contract but most are for about 1k. If the GF has a deductible greater than 1k and hasn't met it then she would be liable for the full 1k. If she had met her deductible she would probably have a co-pay (depending on her policy). Co-pays are usually 20% for ER if they are applicable.

As for why hospital costs are so expensive in the first place, there's a lot of reasons. It mostly comes down to the contracts the hospitals have with the insurance companies and what Medicare will pay for services. Most insurance company contracts come down to paying percentages or case rates that end up with the hospital paid pennies on the dollar. The reason the hospitals need to have contracts with the insurers in the first place is that if they don't, the hospital is out of network and the patients would end up footing the bills. The patients then can't/won't pay and stop coming, so the hospital closes. It's pretty much the same with Medicare, only there's no contract and the government just straight up says what it will pay. There's no negotiating with CMS. This situation has locked all parties in a vicious cycle causing prices to go ever higher. If anyone is to blame for this sorry state of affairs it's the insurance companies since they started the cycle.
